- When sentiment is negative and forecast is rising, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overcorrection.  
- After a sharp price spike, model tends to overshoot — cap forecast at +10% above recent peak for 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment is consistently negative over 3+ days, model underestimates downside risk — add 2–5% buffer to forecast.  
- Model often overreacts to short-term sentiment swings — smooth 3-day moving average before final forecast.  
- In low-sentiment periods, model underestimates mean reversion — adjust forecast upward by 1–3% if price is below 30-day moving average.  
- Forecast horizon >14 days: model tends to overestimate volatility — reduce forecast by 2–4% for long-term horizons.
